events.factual_description: SHAG presents A Tribute to Miles Davis at BLUES ALLEY JAPAN in Meguro, Tokyo on Monday, September 28, 2026, with separate 5:00 PM and 8:00 PM sets. The lineup is SUGIZO on guitar/violin, KenKen on bass, Shinpei Ruike on trumpet, Kazuhiro Bessho on keyboards, Chihiro Matsuura on drums and Kenji Yoshiura on percussion. SUGIZO's official schedule and BLUES ALLEY JAPAN frame the performance within Miles Davis's 2026 centennial and on the 35th anniversary of his September 28, 1991 death. The venue states that Miles himself performed there for its opening, and the event is explicitly conceived not as repertory reconstruction but as SHAG's response to Miles's exploratory spirit through the band's current blend of jazz, rock, dub, funk, ambient and noise.

en.why_it_matters: The hook is not another Miles repertory night. SHAG already works in a language of psychedelic jam, jazz-rock, dub, funk, ambient space and noise, so the idea is to answer Miles's appetite for reinvention with the band's own vocabulary. The setting sharpens that argument: BLUES ALLEY JAPAN ties its history directly to a Miles opening performance, and this lands on September 28 during his centennial year, exactly 35 years after his death. SUGIZO's guitar/violin, KenKen's bass and Shinpei Ruike's trumpet give the project enough instrumental personality that the tribute can plausibly become transformation rather than imitation.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the two sets if your Tokyo dates overlap, especially if the Miles centennial, Japanese fusion and psychedelic improvisation are part of the listening thread. The exact-date and venue history make this more compelling than a routine tribute, but I would still place a truly singular master, premiere or farewell above it if the calendar forces a choice.

es.why_it_matters: El gancho no es otra noche de repertorio de Miles. SHAG ya trabaja desde una mezcla de jam psicodélico, jazz-rock, dub, funk, espacio ambient y ruido, así que la idea es responder al impulso de reinvención de Miles con un vocabulario propio. El lugar vuelve el argumento más preciso: BLUES ALLEY JAPAN liga su historia directamente con una actuación de Miles en su apertura, y la fecha cae el 28 de septiembre, en pleno centenario, exactamente 35 años después de su muerte. La guitarra/violín de SUGIZO, el bajo de KenKen y la trompeta de Shinpei Ruike le dan suficiente identidad instrumental para que el tributo pueda convertirse en transformación y no en imitación.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los dos sets si coincide con tus días en Tokio, sobre todo si el centenario de Miles, la fusión japonesa y la improvisación psicodélica forman parte del hilo. La fecha exacta y la historia del venue la vuelven mucho más interesante que un tributo rutinario, aunque si el calendario obliga a escoger pondría por delante a un maestro realmente escaso, un estreno o una despedida.
